messages:
maria.g: FYI compliance just asked us to keep auth logs for 7 years for EU customers. wondering how painful this is for SIEM exports + KMS rotation.
chen: 7 years = ~2555 days. storage cost aside, main pain is key lifecycle and access scope. :thinking_face:
sam_o: can we tier them? keep 90d hot in SIEM, then cold archive in long-term bucket with different key and stricter access.
anya: are we allowed to store customer-identifiable fields that long? GDPR-ish concerns. we need legal signoff for retention > standard 1yr.
maria.g: legal looped in. they want a defensible audit trail for investigations, but also want encryption-at-rest + least-privilege access. they asked for a proposed design by EOD.
sec-bot: Ticket created: C-4521 - "EU auth log 7yr retention request". Assigned: eng-security. Link: https://internal/incidents/C-4521 :ticket:
chen: proposal sketch: 1) keep 90d in primary SIEM index (current key) 2) move older events to archived-siem bucket encrypted with a rotation-only CMK and restricted IAM 3) expose read-only masked views for analysts via a proxy service.
sam_o: for the proxy service, we should separate roles: ops_read (day-to-day), forensics_read (sensitive unmasked), and forensics_approve (can request de-mask). approvals go to a two-person oncall from sec.
anya: that approval flow needs auditable steps — ideally a signed request that triggers a short-lived data decryption session. otherwise analysts could just copy data out.
chen: technical KMS note: re-wrapping on rotation will be expensive for large archive. prefer wrap-with-new-key-on-write migration when records are accessed, or scheduled background rewrap if compliance requires single-key encryption timeline.
maria.g: legal wants all archived logs to be recoverable for investigations without hitting cross-org approvals except in extreme cases. that contradicts least-privilege aim a bit.
sam_o: possible compromise: keep envelope key for the archive that security owns; on-demand unwrap requires a ticket and 2 approvers. logs stay encrypted with customer-specific context masked by default.
anya: need mapping of which fields are considered PII for masking. i'll draft a small spec.
chen: also: SIEM export pipeline needs a flag so that when export target == long-term-archive we add header "x-archive-ttl: 2555d" and route to archival key manager.
maria.g: sample retention config I was thinking of:

```
{
  "dataset": "auth_events",
  "retention_days": 2555,
  "hot_window_days": 90,
  "archive_bucket": "s3://redwood-archives/eu/auth/",
  "kms_key": "projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/siem/cryptoKeys/arch_7y",
  "access_model": "masked_view_default",
  "unmask_approval_flow": "2_person_approve"
}
```

sam_o: that looks fine. add a note about searchability: we should keep indexed tokens (user_id hash, event_type) in the hot window and minimal index for archive to save cost.
chen: ops question: how do we handle key rotation for arch_7y without breaking ability to decrypt older segments? need key version map in metadata for each object.
anya: yes include key_version_id in object metadata and a small index for object->key mapping. can store the mapping in KMS-proxy DB (encrypted) so only sec-team can read it.
maria.g: timeline: legal signoff expected tomorrow, engineering design by Friday, POC of archive + proxy next sprint. can we get rough cost/effort estimates now?
sam_o: effort: small POC 2w, full integration 4-6w with testing and IAM reviews. cost: depends on archive size; will estimate after sampling.
chen: action items: 1) anya draft PII mask spec 2) sam POC plan for proxy + role model 3) me outline KMS rotation strategy and metadata mapping 4) maria consolidate for legal.
anya: i'll start doc and add examples of masked vs unmasked fields.
sec-bot: Reminder: please add RFC to docs repo under security/retention within 48h.
maria.g: thanks team. ping me if you hit blockers with legal or infra. :thumbsup:
sam_o: +1. i'll spin up a tiny bucket and test rewrap cost numbers tomorrow.
chen: tagging @maria.g for final review on the retention config before I post RFC.
maria.g: will do. closing thread after RFC draft.
